terra.problem: The army is presented as a possible reason Ben-hadad does not ask nicely. The text does not give that reason, and marking a reason as a guess does not permit adding it.
Calling Ahab's reply a quick yes adds a speed the text does not give.
The text calls them elders but does not say they are older leaders.
Saying the crowd has had enough attributes a feeling to the elders and people without marking it as Papa Dorin's guess.
The explanation presents Samaria turning to dust as an outcome rather than Ben-hadad's threat. His oath says there would not be enough dust remaining for each man to have a handful.
The text does not say Samaria is making plans while the kings are drinking.
The explanation is flat and repetitive, ending with a generic observation about tents and cups.
The text says Ben-hadad's servants stationed themselves against the city, not that the whole army moved.
Saying the army goes into Ahab's hand, not home to Aram, rules out a destination the passage does not address.
Saying the troops march out with Ahab adds his presence to that march. The text says the army follows the young officers.
The text does not say that no one is ready for a march. The Israelite troops are already marching out.
The passage says each of the young officers struck down his opponent. 'Each of Israel's men' extends that action to all the Israelite troops.
The text says the Arameans fled, but does not say they had no time to regroup or that none got back into formation.
